concepts.def: Cardinal and Lord Chancellor 1515-29; fell from power after failing to secure Henry's divorce from Catherine of Aragon.
Chief minister 1532-40 who engineered the break with Rome and Dissolution of Monasteries; executed July 1540.
Law declaring Henry VIII Supreme Head of the Church of England, breaking from papal authority in Rome.
1536-40 closure of 800 religious houses; transferred huge wealth and lands to Crown.
Major northern rebellion led by Robert Aske against religious changes; 30,000 marched in Yorkshire before being crushed.
Lavish diplomatic meeting near Calais between Henry VIII and Francis I of France organised by Wolsey.
